Exact and reference solutions Compare with the known bimodal Gaussian mixture’s analytic density, moments, declared CDF points and positive occupancy, and check diagnostics against independent ArviZ references. Distinguish trapping from diagnostic limitations; reassuring local diagnostics do not guarantee global mixing. References and results of execution examples Supplementary execution example Multimodal MCMC: trapping, false reassurance and a global proposal Compare with analytic moments, seven declared CDF points and positive occupancy. Record per-chain occupancies/transitions, rank/folded split Rhat, bulk/tail/mean and mode-indicator ESS, and within-only ACF/ESS. Dispersed trapped chains can have a good pooled distribution yet fail between-chain diagnostics; same-mode chains can have reassuring Rhat yet fail the known target. A control scenario passes when its intended failure is detected. CDF error is a declared-point maximum, not whole-line KS distance or an IID-test p-value. Use these commands in the working directory specified by the execution guide after extracting the ZIP. A command may execute several cases in the package. python -m pip install -r requirements.txt python -m pytest -q python run.py --input inputs.json --output output Validation limits An educational fixed-seed, finite-budget experiment. The local Gaussian RW is theoretically irreducible MH; finite-time trapping is not called a nonergodic algorithm. Small Rhat, large ESS and pooled-CDF agreement cannot rule out undiscovered modes. Symmetry-informed reflection is not a generic multimodal solver. No quantum calculations.
